newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jailed Indonesian labour leader hospitalised.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Indonesian labour leader hospitalised.

text.p: Jailed Indonesian labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan, who is on trial for subversion, has been admitted to a private hospital in Jakarta, family members and a union official said on Sunday.

"He has been admitted to the Cikini hospital in a serious condition. He is not yet stable and we expect him to be there perhaps another three or four days," an official from the unrecognised union told Reuters.
Family members confirmed that Pakpahan had been admitted to the hospital on Saturday suffering from vertigo.
The union official, who requested anonymity, said Pakpahan was able to receive visitors but was under a permanent watch of four guards from the Cipinang prison.
The admission comes after weeks of battles in an out of court to have him admitted to a private hospital and examined by his own doctor rather than government doctors at the Jakarta police hospital.

Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was detained in July and charged with subversion, which carries the death penalty, following riots in the capital Jakarta on July 27.
However, when his trial began in December, prosecutors did not mention directly the July riots. Instead they accused Pakpahan of a number of subversive acts in his writings and speeches.
Human rights lawyers say they cannot recall anyone charged with subversion in Indonesia escaping conviction.
Last Thursday, Pakpahan failed to attend a scheduled hearing of his case because he was sick. It was unclear whether he would be well enough to attend his next scheduled hearing on March 13.
Pakapahan was jailed in 1994 on charges that he incited racial rioting in the north Sumatran city of Medan in April that year after a series of strikes.
He was freed on appeal and his conviction was quashed by the Supreme Court. But the conviction was reinstated in a highly unusual decision last year after his arrest on the subversion charge.
